'''Version 0.9.9.7''' is a test build available through Steam's <code>next_version_tester</code> branch, not a released 1.0 version. The wiki's latest stable reference remains [[Version 0.9.6.5|0.9.6.5]]. Tester-only item pages and sections are labeled explicitly; stable stats and acquisition tables still describe 0.9.6.5.

The developer's Discord announcement supplied to the wiki describes this as the intended final 1.0 version undergoing stability testing. Its release date is unconfirmed: the supplied message has no timestamp or link, and no Steam announcement identifies 0.9.9.7. The comparison below is between 0.9.6.5 and the installed 0.9.9.7 tester.

'''Spoilers:''' this page names enemies and describes the newly accessible cave.

== Tester additions ==
=== Items ===
The installed tester adds '''13 item definitions''' compared with 0.9.6.5, rather than the announcement's approximate 20. Four previously named but undefined items now have definitions; nine additional names are new.

{| class="wikitable"
! Group !! Tester-only items
|-
| Shields and armor || [[Iron Shield]], [[Iron Chestplate]], [[Steel Buckler]], [[Wooden Shield]]
|-
| Weapons || [[Battle Hammer]], [[Halfmoon Axe]], [[War Mace]], [[Hand Sickle]], [[Sturdy Shortbow]]
|-
| Clothing || [[Well Tailored Socks]], [[Laughable Socks]], [[Well Tailored Shirt]], [[Well Tailored Pants]]
|}

[[Sturdy Shortbow]] can be crafted through the player's crafting menu: 2 [[Twine]], 2 [[Branch (Trollgnarl)]] and 10 [[Spider Silk]] produce one bow for a base cost of 8 AP. The other 12 additions have no crafting recipe in their definitions. Declared item values are not evidence that merchants stock them.

General random treasure can now consider item definitions through the new bow, but normal item-type exclusions, cell-size limits and value budgets still apply. This is not a guarantee that every new item appears in every treasure pool.

=== Newly accessible cave ===
During generation of new areas, eligible ordinary small-cave candidates can now become the special entrance leading to the existing spider cave. The replacement roll is approximately one third '''of those eligible candidates''', after ordinary cave selection and collision checks; it is not a one-third chance for every cave or area.

Areas already saved with terrain are loaded without this generation step. Explore previously ungenerated areas or start a new game; revisiting an already generated area does not add the entrance.

[[Mirk Lurker]] and [[Deathlob]], the cave layout, webs and treasure were already defined in 0.9.6.5. This tester makes the entrance assignment functional; it does not add two new enemy definitions or change their base stats. A displayed in-game name for this cave is unconfirmed. Cave-like classification includes it, but the separate dungeon-like classification does not, so dungeon-wide behavior should not be assumed.

In particular, the cave's HUD keeps the weather/day clock rather than the underground display. The temperature and drying calculation uses the current weather temperature rather than the fixed underground 0.35 value. Cave tiles alone do not imply underground exposure rules.

== Tester changes ==
=== Cooking ===
[[Grilled Spider Meat]] is now offered by a burning [[Campfire]]. Its recipe remains 1 [[Spider Meat]] into 1 grilled meat for 2.4 base AP. It is not added to the [[Survivor's Field Kit]] menu.

=== Rafts ===
[[Finish Raft]] has a base action cost of 6 AP instead of 6.4. Its context menu now offers Push, Pull and Board. Push and Pull each cost 6 AP. Push targets one tile (16 pixels) away and requires a free destination; the AP is spent before that check, so a blocked push still costs AP. Pull first moves the player 3 pixels away and brings the raft toward the player's resulting position; push nudges the player 3 pixels toward it.

Direct boarding requires being within 8 pixels; otherwise interaction opens the raft menu. Boarding enters the rafting state. The raft moves toward its target over time rather than teleporting, and its water bobbing is disabled while frozen. In-progress push/pull destinations are not saved, so their continuation after reloading is unconfirmed.

=== Honey, trees and ground cover ===
Outside-area [[Honey]] replenishment now has an outer 50% gate before the existing checks. All trees are activated for the area's count; existing limits remain: fewer than 4.25 special resources overall, fewer than one per tree, at least 12 branches, and the nested 1.5% tree roll before selecting a branch plus its other conditions. This is not a 50% chance per tree and does not impose a minimum distance between honey-bearing trees.

Tree branch death chance is quartered within the 16-pixel view margin. Outside that margin, activated trees with average branch life at most 0.01 have a 1% removal roll per check. Log placement is conditional: nearby mossy-log tiles are counted within 128 pixels, the count reduces the attempted line length, and placement is attempted only when the count is positive. Room bounds, terrain above water, slope, obstruction and ground-cover checks still apply. The tree is removed even if no logs are placed; '''dead trees do not guarantee replacement logs'''.

Log scattering now checks each candidate's position rather than the line's center. Revisiting outside areas other than Rift-Thorn Mire can also attempt [[Fern]] growth over elapsed days. Elapsed time is capped at 240 hours, with up to 10 day iterations and up to 256 candidate-position searches per iteration; this is not log growth.

=== Outside enemies ===
[[Deathlob]] joins outside spawn selection with a weight of 0.125 in [[Sunken Ancient Ruins]] and 0.1 in the other general outside pool. These are relative selection weights, '''not 12.5% and 10% encounter probabilities'''; ordinary population caps and other spawn gates still apply.

== Fixes and smaller changes ==
'''Not in the announcement:'''

* When no sickness effect is present, the accidental 0.16 wellbeing increase is removed and sickness time is reset. Existing sickness levels retain their 1%, 2% and 3% penalties.
* Poison damage-number opacity now follows its cell opacity.
* Fuel searches exclude equipped items, while tool searches still include them. Closing a submenu clears its secondary selected slot.
* Placement's container-collision check applies only to tiles within 8 pixels of the proposed placement point, not as a general container scan over the whole footprint.
* Jump completion and bobbing, frame-rate-scaled motion offsets, tree-part sampling and tree highlighting receive adjustments. Being draw culling is a rendering change, not enemy despawning.
* English UI adds Push, Pull and Board; the item-name list adds nine names. English Bestiary, Nature and Keys are unchanged. Missing translated UI, item and bestiary keys can be filled without replacing existing translations; no new German language folder is added.
* The Latin font gains Ä, Ö, ß, ä and ö; the Chinese font is unchanged.

The developer item selector expands, but it is not a normal player feature. No achievement-unlock change or new player-save field is confirmed by this comparison.
